styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Maratha forts, old wadas and the Aga Khan Palace.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Misal pav, thali and bakery chai runs.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Hill forts, gardens and green getaways nearby.

stays.why: Leafy lanes, cafés and restaurants. Good for food and nightlife; a short ride to the centre.
Central and close to FC Road, old-city sights and the river. Easy for first-time sightseeing.
Historic core with markets and cheap eats. Close to the railway station and MG Road.
Closest to the airport, with malls and cafés. Best for early flights or short stays.

food: Try misal pav for breakfast: sprouted beans, spicy gravy and crunchy toppings. Ask for less spice if unsure.
Order a Maharashtrian thali for a full plate: bhakri, sabzi, dal, rice and chutneys.
Pune is famous for its bakeries. Grab chai and a bun maska or a fresh baked good in the afternoon.
Street snacks like vada pav and sabudana khichdi are cheap and easy to find. Prices are low, often ₹20–80.
Look for Parsi and Irani café dishes, and end meals with shrikhand or puran poli when you see them.
more_time: Add a day trip to Sinhagad or Lohagad fort for views and a walk. Go early; check the road and weather on the day.
Spend a morning at the Aga Khan Palace and the nearby Gandhi-linked sights if you like history.
Escape the city heat with a half-day trip to a hill spot or garden outside town. Check travel time on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the old city, the Aga Khan Palace and a fort day trip without rushing.

month_notes: Cool and dry. Great for sightseeing and forts. Bring a light layer for evenings.
Warm and dry. Comfortable days; start outdoor sights early.
Hotter and dry. Plan shade and water breaks at midday.
Very hot. Do sights in the morning and evening; stay indoors at peak heat.
Hot with some rain days. Carry water and a light rain layer.
Monsoon starts. Many rain days; keep plans flexible and carry rain gear.
Wettest month. Expect heavy rain; favour indoor sights and short trips.
Still very wet. Check roads before any fort or hill trip.
Rain eases but still frequent. Green hills; carry rain protection.
Rain drops off. Pleasant for sightseeing and day trips.
Dry and mild. One of the best months to visit.
Cool and dry. Good for walking and outdoor plans; evenings are chilly.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical with a hot, dry spring and a strong monsoon from June to September. October to February is the most comfortable.

items.title: Best time: November to February
items.text: Highs around 29–32°C and cool nights near 15–17°C. Ideal for forts, old-city walks and day trips.

items.title: Hot and dry: March to May
items.text: Highs reach 34–37°C with little rain. Sightsee early morning and evening; avoid midday sun.

items.title: Monsoon: June to September
items.text: Many rain days, up to 28 in July. Expect heavy showers; keep plans flexible and carry rain gear.

items.title: Green after the rain
items.text: October still has some rain days but hills and gardens look lush. Good for nature trips.

items.title: Sun protection
items.text: Even in cooler months the sun is strong at midday. Hat, sunscreen and water help.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light cotton clothes, a rain jacket or umbrella in monsoon, and a light layer for cool winter evenings.

transit.best: Use Uber, Ola or autos for most trips; the metro and buses are cheap for longer hops.

modes.text: Two lines: Purple (PCMC to Swargate) and Aqua (Vanaz to Ramwadi). Useful for crossing the city; check the route on the day.
PMPML buses reach most areas. Fares about ₹5–30; day passes cost ₹40–50. Cheap but can be slow.
Everywhere and handy for short trips. Insist on the meter; roughly ₹18 for the first 1.5 km.
Uber and Ola work well across the city. Local radio taxis also operate.
Driving is busy but manageable. Two-wheelers are the local norm; helmets are compulsory. Scooter rental is about ₹200–300 a day for day trips.
Fine in the old city and market areas in cooler months. Use rides for longer hops in the heat.
